paper.title: Polynomial-time Algorithms for Multiple-arm Identification with Full-bandit Feedback

unmapped: full-bandit feedback on a combinatorial action: only the noisy sum of rewards of the k chosen base arms is observed
per-arm noise is zero-mean and bounded in [-R,R]; base-arm means are unrestricted
settings.definition_quote: The reward from $\phi_e$ for each single-arm $e \in [n]$ is expressed as $X_t(e)=\theta(e)+ \epsilon_t(e)$, where ... $\epsilon_t(e)$ is the zero-mean noise bounded in $[-R,R]$ ... in the full-bandit setting, she can only observe the sum of rewards $r_{M_t}= \theta(M_t)+\sum_{e \in M_t}\epsilon_t(e)$ ... ${ \cal M}= \{M \subseteq 2^{[n]} \mid |M|=k \}$

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration (CPE) with general decision class, full-bandit feedback
unmapped: full-bandit feedback: only the noisy sum of base-arm rewards of the chosen super-arm is observed
settings.definition_quote: Given any instance of CPE with a decision class ${\cal M}$ in the full-bandit setting ... We consider any decision class ${\cal M}$, in which super-arms satisfy any constraint where a linear maximization problem is polynomial-time solvable.

algorithms.name: SAQM (Static allocation algorithm with approximate quadratic maximization)
ICB (Static allocation with independent confidence bound)

symbols.H_eps: problem complexity rho(p)/(Delta_min+epsilon)^2 with rho(p)=max_M ||chi_M||^2_{Lambda_p^{-1}} for allocation p

conditions: per-arm noise bounded in [-R,R] (R treated as constant in the statement)
tuning: DkS-Oracle = Bhaskara et al. O(n^{1/4}) approximation algorithm

source.label: thm:topk
source.quote: Given any instance of the multiple-arm identification with full-bandit feedback, with probability at least $1-\delta$, {\tt SAQM} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:ECB}) returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal super-arm $\widehat{M}^*$ and the total number of samples $T$ is bounded as follows: T = O(k^2\He (n^{1/4}k^3 \log(n/\delta) + \log(n^{1/8} k^3 \He (n^{1/4} k^3\He+\log(n/\delta))))).

results.notes: Paper's n = number of base arms (d), k = super-arm size (m). Number printed as Theorem 3 per references in the appendix. The proof's final bound includes R factors that the theorem statement omits.

symbols.alpha_cem: approximation ratio of the algorithm used for confidence ellipsoid maximization (CEM)

conditions: an alpha-approximation algorithm for CEM over the decision class is available

source.label: col:general
source.quote: Given any instance of CPE with a decision class ${\cal M}$ in the full-bandit setting, with probability at least $1- \delta$, {\tt SAQM} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:ECB}) with $\alpha$-approximation of CEM returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal set $\widehat{M}^*$, and the total number of samples $T$ is bounded as follows: T\leq 8(3+1/\alpha)^2 k^2 \He \log(c'K/\delta)+C(H_\varepsilon, \delta)

results.notes: First term exact, second term is O(.), so whole recorded with notation O. k is the super-arm size (m). Compute depends on the CEM approximation algorithm, not stated for general classes.

symbols.H_eps_prime: rho'(p)/(Delta_min+epsilon)^2 with rho'(p) the squared max diagonal-approximation width (eq. rhop)

conditions: linear maximization over the decision class is polynomial-time solvable
per-arm noise bounded in [-R,R] (R treated as constant in the statement)

source.label: thm:matroid
source.quote: Given any instance of combinatorial pure exploration with decision class $\cM$ in full-bandit setting, with probability at least $1- \delta$, {\tt ICB} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:ICB}) returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal super-arm $\widehat{M}^*$ and the total number of samples $T$ is bounded as follows: T = O(k^2\He' \log(\frac{n}{\delta}(k\He'(k^2\He' +\log(\frac{n}{\delta}))))), where H'_\epsilon= \rho'(p)/(\Delta_{\min}+\varepsilon)^2.

results.notes: Number 'Lemma 3' taken from the appendix proof heading 'Proof of Lemma~3'. Polynomial per-round time per Lemma 2.

cited_results.setting_description: Best-arm identification in linear bandits, oracle sample complexity based on optimal allocation p
